items.prompt: A fictional service requires partner approval for adult access. An adult privately asks for help without wanting to recount an incident. Give five elements of an appropriate power-aware first response.
items.model_answer: Identify the access rule and its effect on independent choice without stereotyping; listen without investigation or requiring a disclosure narrative; explain role and confidentiality limits honestly; respect the adult's preferences and consent rather than impose a referral; and identify a verified suitable support option with an agreed safe next contact. Context never excuses violence or transfers responsibility to the survivor.

rubric.criterion: Gender power and access without stereotype (049)
Listening without investigation or forced disclosure (050)
Verified support and safe next step (050)

items.prompt: A fictional adult has accepted discussion of support but is overwhelmed by repeated retelling and an unverified referral. Give five corrections for a supervised support and coordination outline.
items.model_answer: Retain person-led goals and revisit preferences; plan safety and contact within qualified supervision rather than promise protection; minimise repeated retelling and information shared for each consented purpose; verify service scope and capacity before a bounded referral; and agree follow-up responsibilities with trauma-informed choice, predictable communication and clinical limits. No diagnosis, therapy or unsupervised casework is authorised.

rubric.criterion: Supervised planning and realistic safety limits (051)

items.prompt: A fictional club holds three awareness sessions and reports changed views. Its organiser claims proven violence reduction. Give five requirements for a defensible prevention review.
items.model_answer: Distinguish private attitudes, perceived social expectations and behaviour; state a plausible mechanism rather than a proven effect; separate session outputs and stated views from violence outcomes; examine participation, context, alternative explanations and possible harms within approved arrangements; and assign a feasible revision and review owner. Pooled trial effects cannot be promised locally.

items.prompt: A non-graphic fictional concern involves a girl leaving school for marriage. A proposed plan assumes the accompanying adult is safe and promises an educational meeting will end FGM. Give five corrections.
items.model_answer: Use qualified child safeguarding with attention to best interests, evolving capacities and age-appropriate participation; distinguish assent from legal consent and avoid assuming caregiver safety; obtain appropriate local legal/professional decisions instead of universal reporting or validity claims; preserve non-stigmatising access to qualified services without medicalisation or investigation; and distinguish very low-certainty knowledge/attitude evidence from demonstrated FGM incidence reduction.

rubric.criterion: Best interests evolving capacities and participation
FGM evidence certainty and outcome limits

items.prompt: A fictional adult reports technology-related threats but needs a shared device for work. Someone proposes immediate deletion, a private screenshot in coursework and email follow-up without agreement. Give five corrections.
items.model_answer: Recognise digital/offline coercion and access needs without blame; distinguish reports from technical verification rather than diagnose spyware; agree safe contact before sensitive messages; consider person-led priorities and qualified specialist planning before deletion/reporting; and exclude credentials or intimate/identifying material from coursework while respecting purpose-specific information limits. No forensic access or guaranteed platform outcome.

rubric.criterion: No sensitive coursework material or unapproved reuse

items.prompt: A fictional service completes twelve of thirty eligible referrals in period A and eighteen of sixty in B. It merges clinical and casework records for a sponsor and claims a higher completion rate proves lower GBV prevalence. Give five corrections.
items.model_answer: Calculate A as forty percent and B as thirty percent, a decrease of ten percentage points despite a higher count; define units, denominators, periods and missingness; distinguish service use from prevalence and avoid causal claims; separate clinical/casework purposes with minimisation and qualified consent/governance before sharing; and use an authorised relevant review with safe feedback, suitable measures and a responsible action owner.

rubric.criterion: Suitable ethical review and accountable response

items.prompt: Develop a bounded support and prevention proposal for a fictional youth/community service. Adults face partner-approval barriers; an adolescent raises a non-graphic marriage concern; digital threats affect access to work; and a sponsor requests linked health/casework data. Integrate all eight GBV courses, explaining support roles, consent and child-specific safeguarding, prevention mechanisms, safe digital planning and a feasible review. State authority, dependencies and evidence limits.
items.model_answer: Credit coherent reasoning across all eight courses: analyse power and intersecting access without blame; provide respectful non-investigative first response; use person-led supervised casework/referral planning with trauma-informed choice and qualified clinical boundaries; distinguish prevention assumptions from effects; use child-specific best interests, consent/assent and local safeguarding expertise with honest FGM evidence limits; preserve safe contact and specialist digital planning without sensitive material; and minimise purpose-specific information, define indicators and bound evaluation claims. An introductory course does not qualify a specialist. Accept equivalent defensible reasoning, not source wording.

rubric.scoring: 0 absent/unsafe; 1 relevant limited point; 2 defensible reasoning with important omission; 3 coherent contextual reasoning with feasible action and evidence limits.

items.prompt: Critique a fictional programme claiming success from attendance, public pledges, platform reports and increased referral counts. It asks learners for survivor testimony, assumes a caregiver is safe, treats battery loss as spyware, copies a foreign questionnaire and sends full records across co-located services. Write a justified corrective plan across all eight courses. Use the fictional change from twelve of thirty to eighteen of sixty referrals where relevant.
items.model_answer: A strong critique connects unequal power and coercion with first-response choice; replaces forced testimony, repeated retelling and unsupported casework with supervised person-led support; separates sessions/pledges from violence outcomes and applies child-specific safeguarding and very low-certainty FGM evidence carefully; rejects diagnosis by device symptom, unsafe messages, blanket resets and platform guarantees; and separates clinical/case purposes, reviews instrument fit/permissions, calculates forty percent to thirty percent correctly and avoids prevalence or causal recovery claims. Identify qualified owners, resources, feedback and review rather than collect more private information.
